title: CI/CD: Registry-driven attestation + staged performance-profile promotion
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an end-to-end CI/CD flow that produces reproducible model artifacts, creates signed attestations, publishes per-workload performance profiles, and promotes profiles through a staged registry using telemetry-driven canary gates. The flow must handle large model blobs, support both hosted and private onboarding paths, and make promotion decisions deterministic and auditable. Goals: (1) reduce manual steps for model onboarding; (2) ensure every served model has a verifiable provenance chain; (3) enable automated staged rollouts of performance profiles tied to production metrics so runtime rollouts are safer and reversible.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created. Scope includes build reproducibility (deterministic hashes), signing with KMS-backed keys, generation of perf profiles from CI microbenchmarks and end-to-end smoke tests, and a registry API to record provenance and promotion state. Referenced design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Registry+Attestation+and+Profile+Promotion

2026-02-23 - Diego Martinez: Attached proposed pipeline sketch in GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-cicd/issues/58. Key steps: (1) model fetch + normalize, (2) artifact build + chunked upload to S3, (3) compute deterministic digest (build graph + byte-level hash), (4) sign digest with cosign via internal KMS adapter, (5) run perf microbenchmarks matrix (seq len x batch size x token distribution), (6) publish performance profile + raw telemetry to registry, (7) automated promote-if-gated to canary, staged, and production channels.

2026-02-25 - Security (Lina Huang): Reviewed signing approach. Recommendation: use HSM-backed signing for production releases; accept cosign + KMS adapter for developer-flow with an allowlist. Action: add rotation policy and key-scoped signing certs. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-03-01 - Diego Martinez: Spike results attached: GH PR #212 implements digest+cosign integration and prototype registry API. Performance profile schema v2 uploaded to S3 at s3://redwood-model-profiles/profiles/schema-v2.json. Observations: deterministic builds for ONNX/ggml require container-level normalization; PyTorch wheel artifacts had nondeterminism due to timestamped metadata — added strip-step.

2026-03-03 - Alex Kim (Runtime): Noted trade-off: running microbenchmarks in CI increases latency and runner cost. Proposal: run a fast microbenchmark set in CI for gating, then push full benchmark jobs to a dedicated perf cluster before final promotion. This preserves early feedback while keeping CI budget reasonable.

2026-03-05 - Design review (Maya Singh): UX for promotion state in Console — add per-model timeline with artifact signatures, profile variants, and gate decision reason. Also need an 'emergency unpin' button with audit log and rollback link. Filed PM follow-up: PM-814.

2026-03-07 - Diego Martinez: Implemented automated canary gate evaluator. Gate rules are configurable per-project and use production metrics: 95th latency, error-rate, and token-accuracy regressions relative to baseline. Gate thresholds live in registry metadata and evaluated by telemetry-job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-gates/pull/37. Canary job emits decision event and links to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/model-rollouts/canary-telemetry

2026-03-09 - QA (Ravi Patel): Added acceptance tests to run on sample public models and private mirror. Tests assert: signature verified against KMS, digest matches uploaded artifact, profile entries include test matrix metadata, promotion state transitions are idempotent, and rollback restores previous profile pin. Found edge-case: partial upload retry can yield duplicate manifests; fixed by using manifest-level UUID and idempotent POST semantics.

2026-03-10 - Diego Martinez: Merged core pipeline to main (GH PR #251). Next: bake staging traffic for 48 hours and watch canary gate metrics. Follow-ups: add HSM signing ops runbook (SEC-ops-112), integrate with dedicated perf cluster for full-profile runs, and create onboarding checklist for external partners (docs/partner-onboard.md).
